chapters.screen: Logistic Regression. Logistic regression adds up weighted inputs and squashes the total into a probability. Watch gradient descent tune four numbers until the 50% boundary separates survivors from the rest as well as a straight cut can.
chapters.spoken: Logistic Regression. Logistic regression adds up weighted inputs and squashes the total into a probability. Watch gradient descent tune four numbers until the 50% boundary separates survivors from the rest as well as a straight cut can.

chapters.screen: Each mark is one passenger: age (x) and fare paid (y, log scale); women on the left, men on the right. Blue dots survived, red crosses did not.
chapters.spoken: Each mark is one passenger: age and fare paid on a log scale; women on the left, men on the right. Blue dots survived, red crosses did not.

chapters.screen: First guess: all weights are 0, so every passenger gets P(survive) = 50% and the maps are grey. Circled passengers are the ones it gets wrong.
chapters.spoken: First guess: all weights are 0, so every passenger gets a 50% chance of survival and the maps are grey. Circled passengers are the ones it gets wrong.

chapters.screen: Each step computes the log loss's gradient over all 627 passengers and moves the weights a little downhill (learning rate 1.5). The boundary is where P(survive) = 50%.
chapters.spoken: Each step computes the log loss's gradient over all 627 passengers and moves the weights a little downhill (learning rate 1.5). The boundary is where the chance of survival is 50%.

chapters.screen: After 60 steps: train accuracy 77%, validation 78%. Largest weight: woman, then fare; smallest: age.
chapters.spoken: After 60 steps: train accuracy 77%, validation 78%. Largest weight: woman, then fare; smallest: age.

chapters.screen: An unseen passenger: scale the inputs, add up bias + weight × input, and squash the total with the sigmoid σ to get a probability, compared with 50%.
chapters.spoken: An unseen passenger: scale the inputs, add up bias plus weight times input, and squash the total with the sigmoid sigma to get a probability, compared with 50%.

chapters.screen: Final exam: the trained model judges all 210 test passengers it has never seen. Wrong calls are circled on the maps and crossed in the grid, grouped by class of travel.
chapters.spoken: Final exam: the trained model judges all 210 test passengers it has never seen. Wrong calls are circled on the maps and crossed in the grid, grouped by class of travel.

chapters.screen: Logistic regression passes a straight-line score through the S-shaped sigmoid, so each sheet is a smooth slope that never leaves the 0–100% range. Height is the model's P(survive), one sheet per sex, seen by a swinging camera.
chapters.spoken: Logistic regression passes a straight-line score through the S-shaped sigmoid, so each sheet is a smooth slope that never leaves the 0 to 100% range. Height is the model's chance of survival, one sheet per sex, seen by a swinging camera.

chapters.screen: About the same: 82% with every input against 81% with age, fare and sex.
chapters.spoken: About the same: 82% with every input against 81% with age, fare and sex.

chapters.screen: Logistic regression turns a weighted sum into a probability; gradient descent finds the weights that make the observed outcomes most likely. Limitation: its boundary is a straight cut in the scaled inputs, so it cannot capture patterns such as 'young boys survived' without extra features.
chapters.spoken: Logistic regression turns a weighted sum into a probability; gradient descent finds the weights that make the observed outcomes most likely. Limitation: its boundary is a straight cut in the scaled inputs, so it cannot capture patterns such as 'young boys survived' without extra features.
